evidence: Dimension weights: task/tests/scoring.toml is byte-identical to the frozen template (diff empty): [gates] render=0.0 constraints=0.0; [weights] functional=0.6 polish=0.2 visual=0.2; [floors] functional=0.05. This matches the SKILL delivery profile and the Internal Quality Checks row 45 annotation (functional 60%). task/tests/tools/score.py sha256 13de2b38...e04e equals the template's: reward = weighted mean of the three scored dimensions, zeroed unless gates pass and functional > 0.05. No 'weight' key in any [judge] block (only criterion-level weights), so dimension weight lives only in scoring.toml as the contract requires. Per-criterion weights: one documented scheme, stated identically in every judge.toml ('# Criterion weights: 1.0 standard, 1.5 important, 2.0 core to the brief (Visual Likert rows are equal).', e.g. task/tests/scored/functional/judge.toml:23). Functional has 44 binary criteria totalling 61.0 (21 at 1.0, 12 at 1.5, 11 at 2.0). The 2.0 rows are hro_refused_put_back, hro_stale_refused, hro_bulk_all_or_none, hro_undo_restores, hro_undo_conflict, hro_live_board, hro_thread_earlier, hro_unread_counts, hro_unread_scrolled_up, hro_drafts and hro_candidate_private. Each maps to a sentence the brief stresses as the hard or core part: instruction.md para 1 says 'the hard part is that nobody's work gets trampled when someone else acts'; para 2 covers put-back with reason, who moved it, all-or-none and undo; para 3 covers live updates within 15 s; para 4 covers earlier messages without losing place, unread counts and drafts; para 5 says candidates 'must never see our internal notes'. The keyboard-focus part of hro_refused_put_back is public (hireops_rules.md:87 'keep my keyboard focus on that card's controls'). All 1.0 rows are real behaviour: basic CRUD/validation (job_open, add_candidate, email rules), role rules and Activity. None is weighted for structure or style, and no criterion carries weight for source layout, file names or tech-stack inspection. Gates carry one binary weight-1 criterion each under all_pass, and score.py gives gates no reward mass. Polish has 5 binary criteria (2,2,2,1.5,2 = 9.5). They test real behaviour (unsaved note and draft surviving live updates, earlier-page place, failed-send recovery, session resume), not cosmetics, so the 0.2 polish share also rewards working functionality. Visual has 5 equal-weight 5-point Likert rows with anchors, which is the only style mass, capped at 0.2. Sanity check of the non-functional maximum (skill procedure): style alone can contribute at most 0.2, the visual share. A gate-passing app with only the basic board features (job_open, add_candidate, add_email_rules, move_one_stage, arrive_bottom, reorder, reject_reason, reopen, notes, restart = 11.5/61 = 0.189 functional) reaches about 0.6*0.189 + 0.2 = 0.31 with perfect visuals. A full-featured but plain app reaches about 0.6 + polish + some visual, so functionality dominates the ranking. Polish mostly needs working live updates, so a dead app cannot farm it. The 0.4 non-functional ceiling and the 0.05 floor are template-fixed policy and are not task-editable. Colderwater lessons checked: lesson 2 (one documented scheme, weights not used to steer the band) holds, because a single 1.0/1.5/2.0 scheme is applied by brief importance. Lessons 12-16 concern other rows, and none changes the weighting. Not measured: the customer-style audit (average weight of failed vs passed criteria, equal-weight recompute) needs a target-model run. raw-evidence-index.json says reward discrimination/ranking and model scores are absent. This row is about the static honesty of the weights, which is fully inspectable, so the missing run is not required evidence here. It is reported for rows 42/runtime records.
